summary.intent: Get the PyPI sealed-file-set PR stack (#232/#233) through CI and review: fix a failing CI compile error in a Linux-only test, then address Codex's review findings on hashless confirmation, stale docs, and memory-heavy hashing.
summary.outcome: Fixed the Linux-gated test compile error and pushed via a non-force rebase onto the rebased remote branch. Then fixed all three Codex findings (streaming hashing via ArtifactDigest::from_reader, narrowed publishing.md contract, updated releasing.md and V1-FINDINGS.md); local `just ci` passed at 92.77% coverage and the commit was pushed, with the new CI run not yet confirmed.

repo: `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs` is `#![cfg(target_os = "linux")]`, so it never compiles on macOS and local `just ci` can pass while Linux CI (Clippy, Coverage, Test Suite) fails on it.
To check a Linux-gated file locally, temporarily remove the `cfg` line and run clippy on it, then restore it.

`ArtifactDigest::from_reader` in callisto-model (`crates/callisto-model/src/release/digest.rs`) is the existing streaming digest helper used by artifact verification and should be reused for hashing files.
The workspace enforces a 90% coverage gate via `just ci`.
Sealed mode requires an index-served sha256; files uploaded in the current run are accepted when the index serves no digest, which keeps private indexes without hashes working.
Python-only generated release workflows remain unsealed and build inside the write-capable release job (tracked as T09).

code.finding: Inventory and sealed-file recheck read whole wheels/sdists with std::fs::read and Sha256::digest; replaced by a streaming file_sha256 helper built on ArtifactDigest::from_reader.
Digest comparison only flags a mismatch when the index supplies a SHA-256, so hashless responses are accepted for files uploaded this run.
Stale text claimed a partial PyPI upload can be mistaken for a complete release; Codex cited line 114 but the actual line was 118.

workflow: Verify external review findings against the code before acting; line numbers in reviews can be off.
When a push is rejected, fetch and inspect the remote commits first; replay only new commits with a rebase and push without force.
Run long `just ci` in the background with output redirected to a log, then inspect the tail and exit code.
Write multi-line commit messages to a file and use `git commit -F` to avoid shell quoting problems.

friction: Local CI on macOS missed a Linux-only compile error, causing a failed CI run on the PR.
The first push was rejected because #231 merged and the remote branch had been rebased with new SHAs.
Codex's cited line number for releasing.md was off (114 vs 118).
open_items: Decision pending for the user: whether a PyPI index serving no sha256 should be an error for files uploaded this run (assistant recommends leaving it accepted).
The new CI run on #233 after the final push was still pending/unverified.
Hosted generated-workflow run (representative build, partial upload, rerun) has not been exercised.
The Linux e2e test has not been run against a real pypiserver/Verdaccio.
Trusted publishing (OIDC) for npm and PyPI is a deferred follow-up.
Python-only workspaces remain unsealed; whether to change that is the user's call.
